details: Owner, 29 Oct: "a" = 3 lanes for relay's development (product features, the container gate kept on top) and 3 for fixes (handover addendum of 29 Oct). The decision lives only in the handover; the lane pick (lib/relay_lanes.py) orders fixes first and offers no feature while a fix can start, so on 30 Oct the front filled 6 of 6 lanes with fixes and asked the owner a question the decision already answered.
Also: plugins/front/hooks/lanes.py
Also: lib/relay_config.py
failing_case: 30 Oct 2026: with 6 lanes all on fixes and feature build-time-gates-on-the-vps-landing-gate-on-the (ip 90) startable, the hook's pick named only fixes; the owner had to recall the decision.
pass_cases: With the setting at 3 and 3 fix lanes running, a free lane is offered to the top feature, not a fix.
With the setting at 0, the pick is as today.
The lanes line shows both counts.
reason: tests/test_lanes_state.py::FeatureSplit::test_free_lane_goes_to_the_top_feature_not_a_fix passes at head and fails at 964f3d57.
findings.summary: The lane pick ignores the owner's 3 and 3 lane split

details: CONFIRMED by reading: _one_lane_per_train (lib/relay_lanes.py:295) builds the train lane with slug None and the rider branches in
`riders`; the count at 349 is `lane.slug and kinds.get(lane.slug) == "feature"`, so riders are never looked at. The rider's item is
still taken (it is not landed), so it is a feature that runs; the brief's rule is "while fewer than that many feature lanes run".
The kinds map is keyed by slug, but a lane is a branch: the right key is taken_by -> kinds of the items that branch took.
Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: grep -n 'feature_running = sum' lib/relay_lanes.py -> 349: ... if lane.slug and kinds.get(lane.slug) == "feature"
lanes_state 331-333: a branch that took two items is one lane, Lane(branch, item["slug"]) of the first item only
failing_case: Lanes 6, feature_lanes 3. Running: wt/f1, wt/f2 (features) and wt/f3 (feature) whose branch has been merged into the open train
wt/train-x; plus 2 fix lanes. _one_lane_per_train replaces wt/f3 with Lane("wt/train-x", None, ("wt/f3",)); line 349 counts only
lane.slug, so feature_running = 2. Now: with 1 free lane and a fix (ip 99) and a feature (ip 80) startable, the pick is the feature
and the line says "(3 of 3 fix lanes, 2 of 3 feature lanes)". Should be: feature_running = 3, the free lane goes to the fix, the
line says "(2 of 3 fix lanes, 3 of 3 feature lanes)".
The same miscount happens for a branch that took a fix first and a feature second (Lane keeps the first item's slug only).
fix_hint: Build branch -> set of kinds from open_items with state taken (taken_by), and count a lane as a feature lane when any of
(lane.branch,) + lane.riders took a feature. Add a test with a train rider (the file already has train helpers).
pass_cases: 1. The case above: State.feature_running == 3 and picks == [the fix].
2. Three feature lanes on their own branches, no train, split 3: feature_running == 3, a free lane goes to the top fix (as today's test_running_feature_counts_against_the_quota for split 1).
3. A train whose riders are all fixes: feature_running == 0; split 3 with a startable feature: the feature is picked first.
4. A worktree with no item (Lane slug None, no riders): not counted as a feature lane.
findings.summary: a feature that rides a merge train (or shares a branch with a fix) is not counted as a running feature, so the pick offers one feature lane too many and the line misreports the split

details: CONFIRMED by reading: git grep feature_lanes finds only .claude/kit.toml and lib/relay_lanes.py. An earlier check of this same
paragraph (.relay/checks/04446318... and 50d5632d..., pass case 3) required every [front] setting to be named where kit.toml settings
are documented, so the project treats this as part of a settings change. Principle 10 (works for a newcomer): the agent user learns
relay from its own texts. A skill text edit falls under the batched paid run, which costs nothing extra per change.
Size: 10 minutes.
evidence: SKILL.md:186-188: "The hooks print the pick as one line ...: the top of the queue order, skipping ..."
failing_case: A fresh front session on relay (kit.toml feature_lanes = 3) sees "Lanes: 3 of 6 running (3 of 3 fix lanes, 0 of 3 feature lanes);
design: ft1 (feature, ip 90), start: fa (fix, ip 99)". Its skill (SKILL.md:186-188) says the pick is "the top of the queue order" and
rules/queue.md says every fix before every feature; nothing it reads names feature_lanes. Now: it has no text saying why a feature
outranks a fix, nor how to change the split (the owner's question "how do I make it 4 and 2" cannot be answered from relay's texts).
Should be: the skill's [front] settings list names feature_lanes (default 0, 0..lanes, the lanes kept for features) and the pick
paragraph says features take the kept lanes first.
fix_hint: Add feature_lanes to the SKILL.md [front] settings sentence and one clause to the pick paragraph.
pass_cases: 1. SKILL.md's "Settings under [front]" sentence names `feature_lanes` with default 0, bound 0..lanes and what it does (artifact line).
2. SKILL.md's pick paragraph says that, while fewer feature lanes run than feature_lanes, the free lane goes to the top startable feature first (artifact line).
3. The three existing settings lines stay as they are.
reason: plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md:187 and :198 now describe feature_lanes and the split.
findings.summary: the front skill still says the pick is the top of the queue order and lists three [front] settings; feature_lanes and the split in the line are not documented where the front reads them

details: CONFIRMED by reading the six FeatureSplit tests: five pass features= explicitly; test_setting_is_read_from_kit_toml_and_clamped
checks feature_lanes_setting alone and one lanes_state call whose expected 0 equals the default. Correct today, unguarded.
Size: 5 minutes.
failing_case: Replace `feature_lanes_setting(main, capacity) if features is None else ...` at lib/relay_lanes.py:347 with `0 if features is None
else ...`: every FeatureSplit test still passes (they pass features= directly; the one kit.toml-driven lanes_state call uses "x",
whose expected value is 0 either way). The hook calls lanes_state(root, quiet) without features, so the owner's setting would be
dead and no test would say so. Should: a test fails.
fix_hint: Change the last assertion to seed feature_lanes = 3 and assert feature_split == 3 (and a feature-first pick).
pass_cases: 1. kit.toml "[front]\nfeature_lanes = 3\n", 3 fixes running, limit 6, fa (fix ip 99) and ft1 (feature ip 90) startable, lanes_state(main, now=NOW, limit=6) without features: picks start with ft1 and feature_split == 3.
2. No kit.toml: feature_split == 0 and picks as today.
findings.summary: no test drives lanes_state from kit.toml with a non-zero split, so the path the hook uses passes with the read disabled

details: CONFIRMED by reading feature_lanes_setting (110-119) against setting_note (107). The brief gave "bound 0..lanes" without saying how
out-of-bounds is handled; the file's convention for its other settings is "the default, and the line says so". Clamping to the lanes
turns a "3 and 3" into "all features first" when the lanes drop, which is the opposite of the owner's split. Principle 10.
Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: lib/relay_lanes.py:107: return f"{key} {value} is out of bounds {low}-{high}: {default} is used"
failing_case: kit.toml feature_lanes = 3 and the project's lanes lowered to 2 (projects.toml): the value is clamped to 2, every lane is kept for
features and the line says "(... of 0 fix lanes, ... of 2 feature lanes)" with no note that 3 was out of bounds. feature_lanes = "3"
(a string) silently gives 0, no split. Should: like setting_note for lanes_line_items, the line names the value that was not used.
fix_hint: Return the note beside the value (as setting_note does) and pass it to line(); or use the default 0 when out of bounds, with the note.
pass_cases: 1. feature_lanes = 3, lanes 2: the line ends with a note that feature_lanes 3 is out of bounds 0-2 (whichever value the fix uses is stated).
2. feature_lanes = "x": the line notes it is not a whole number and 0 is used.
reason: lib/relay_lane_features.py:23-26 returns 0 with a note; test_out_of_bounds_is_said_in_the_line passes.
findings.summary: an out-of-bounds or malformed feature_lanes is clamped or zeroed silently, unlike lanes_line_items which says so in the line

details: CONFIRMED by reading: fix count = len(running) - feature_running. Misleading text only; the pick is unaffected. Size: 10 minutes.
evidence: lib/relay_lanes.py:416: f" ({len(state.running) - state.feature_running} of {state.setting - state.feature_split} fix lanes, "
failing_case: Lanes 6, split 3: 3 fix lanes and one design worktree with no queue item (counted as a lane while active). The line says
"(4 of 3 fix lanes, 0 of 3 feature lanes)". Should: the no-item lane is not called a fix lane (e.g. "3 of 3 fix lanes, 0 of 3
feature lanes, 1 without an item").
fix_hint: Count fix lanes as lanes whose items are fixes; say the rest apart or leave them out of both counts.
pass_cases: 1. The case above: the fix count is 3 and the no-item lane is named apart.
2. Only fix lanes running: the line is as test_line_shows_both_counts expects.
findings.summary: the line counts every non-feature lane, a no-item worktree included, as a fix lane
